report.source_text: Physical examination showed that best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) of counting finger at one and three meters in the right and left eyes respectively. Average repeated IOP measured by I- care tonometer was 12 mmHg for right eye and 11 mmHg in the left eye. Pupils were equal in size and reactive to light, there was no relative afferent pupillary defect. Horizontal corneal diameter was 14mm (Figure 1) in both eyes with stromal opacities and Haab's striae (Figure 2). Anterior chambers were deep and gonioscopy revealed wide open angles in both eyes. There was iridodonesis, phacodonesis, as well as superiorly and nasally subluxated cataract lenses in both eyes. The cataract in the right eye was denser.

On 2nd post-operative week, the right eye BCVA was 6/36 and poor vision was explained by amblyopia. After one month the IOP was normal, but intraocular lens (IOL) was dislocated and BCVA decreased to 6/60.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Subluxated cataract of both eyes (denser on right) with spontaneously arrested primary congenital glaucoma
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 32-year-old male from North Shewa, Ethiopia presented in June 2019 with a 2-year worsening of vision reduction that had been present since childhood, along with large eyes noted since childhood. Clinical examination revealed bilateral superiorly and nasally subluxated cataracts (denser on right) with iridodonesis and phacodonesis. Intraocular pressures were normal (12 mmHg OD, 11 mmHg OS) with wide open angles on gonioscopy. Corneal findings included stromal opacities, Haab's striae, and 14mm diameter bilaterally—all consistent with prior congenital glaucoma. Optic disc examination showed pink rim with 0.6 vertical cup-to-disc ratio bilaterally and no nerve fiber layer loss. Visual fields were normal. Biometric measurements showed central corneal thickness of 466um (OD) and 467um (OS), and axial length of 30.3mm (OD) and 29.9mm (OS). The patient underwent manual small incision cataract surgery on the right eye, with post-operative BCVA of 6/36 at 2 weeks (attributed to amblyopia), but IOL dislocation occurred by 1 month with BCVA declining to 6/60 and IOP remaining normal.
